identity.real_world_identity_notes: The observation identifies the AMG-prepared Mercedes-Benz 190 E 2.5-16 Evolution II DTM touring car used in the 1992 Deutsche Tourenwagen-Meisterschaft. Both this record and mercedes-benz-190e-2-5-16-evo-ii-dtm are Group A race cars, confirmed by the maintainer; the earlier note here described that record as a road-going homologation special, which it is not and does not claim to be. They are kept apart as two race specifications rather than road against race: the other record is the 1990 car with a five-speed dogleg Getrag, and this is the 1992 AMG car described by period sources as a six-speed straight-toothed race gearbox. Gear count is the specification difference that keeps them separate. Neither record inherits controls from the other, and if a source shows the two seasons ran the same gearbox they should be merged. Mercedes-Benz describes the Evo II road car as the homologation basis for the DTM touring car and records the 1992 championship success; period/technical secondary evidence describes the 1992 DTM car as a six-speed straight-toothed race car shifted at full throttle without clutch use for upshifts. The exact selector gate, gearbox construction category, launch procedure, downshift clutch/blip procedure, automatic cut/blip behavior, and real wheel-rim topology are not established by the reviewed sources.

Mercedes-Benz's official history identifies the 190 E 2.5-16 Evolution II as the homologation basis for the DTM touring car, dates the race debut to 1990, and records the 1992 title season. Auto Bild's exact 1992 DTM article identifies the AMG-prepared car and reports its six-speed straight-toothed gearbox and full-throttle clutchless shifting. The existing repository record is separately identified as a 1990 homologation special with five-speed synchromesh dogleg controls, so merging the 1992 race specification into it would mix distinct real-world configurations.
